title: Packaging, install/upgrade, CI coverage and remote parts
owns: scripts/package/**, packaging/**, sidecar/uia/ember_uia.ps1, .github/workflows/*.yml (triggers and jobs), app/main/remote/runtime-download.ts, app/main/remote/ssh-config.ts

findings.title: An install path containing a literal % makes every settings/IPC call throw "URI malformed"
findings.area: paths with special characters / first run
findings.scenario: Someone extracts the Windows zip to a folder such as D:\Tools\100% Free\Ember (or runs an AppImage from a folder with a % in its name). BrowserWindow.loadFile does not percent-encode the % in the file URL. isTrustedSender() then calls decodeURIComponent on the sender URL, which throws URIError. Every IPC handler guarded by it fails: ember:get-status, agent:status, agent:conversation, voice:status, targets:list, ember:activity and ember:presence. The windows open but stay dead: no status, no sign-in, no settings. Nothing explains why.
findings.evidence: I staged the Linux tree and ran a copy at ".../Tools C# 100% (x86) & Zoë's/Ember/ember". The log has "Error occurred in handler for 'ember:get-status': URIError: URI malformed at decodeURIComponent at isTrustedSender (main.cjs)", 13 handler errors in all, 7 distinct channels. The same tree at ".../Tools C# (x86) & Zoë's/Ember" (spaces, #, &, ', parentheses and non-ASCII, no %) has 0 errors and shows its window. The only decodeURIComponent in app/ is windows.ts:138. A related nit: autostart.ts execArg (lines 25-29) does not double a % in Exec=, which the Desktop Entry spec requires.
findings.fix: Make isTrustedSender total. Wrap the decode in try/catch and return false on a throw, or better, compare against pathToFileURL(appDir).href + "/renderer/" instead of decoding. Add a unit case with "100%" and "50%AB" in trusted-sender.test.ts. Escape % as %% in execArg.

findings.title: Windows: the UI Automation bridge compiles its C# with Add-Type -Path, which treats [ and ] in the install path as wildcards
findings.area: paths with special characters / Windows helper
findings.scenario: A user extracts Ember into a folder with square brackets, for example C:\Users\Jane [Work]\Apps\Ember or D:\Tools [portable]\Ember. The bridge reads $PSScriptRoot\ember_uia.cs with [IO.File]::ReadAllBytes, which is literal and works. Both Add-Type calls then use -Path, so PowerShell resolves [Work] as a character class and finds no file. The cached-build branch falls back to memory, which fails the same way, and Write-Fatal reports "Cannot find path". Ember can then never read apps. The doctor's Accessibility helper row fails with a path error that does not mention brackets.
findings.evidence: Source reading only; no Windows host here and pwsh is not installed. Add-Type's -Path is documented to accept wildcards, and -LiteralPath exists for exactly this. ember_uia.ps1:78 and :95 both use `Add-Type -Path $source`. The sibling askpass compile (askpass-win.ts) avoids the problem by using -TypeDefinition with ReadAllText.
findings.fix: Use `Add-Type -LiteralPath $source` in both places (Windows PowerShell 5.1 has it). Add a W-series integration case that stages Ember under a folder named "a [b]".

findings.title: AppImage doctor reports FAIL "Sandbox" on user-namespace-off hosts, with a fix for files that do not exist in an AppImage
findings.scenario: On a hardened RHEL 8 host (user.max_user_namespaces=0) the AppImage's AppRun deliberately starts Ember with --no-sandbox, so Ember runs. The user then runs `Ember-0.1.0-x86_64.AppImage doctor`. The doctor probes only user namespaces and a setuid chrome-sandbox next to the binary, which an AppImage cannot have, so it prints "FAIL Sandbox ... fix: sudo chown root:root /opt/ember/chrome-sandbox && sudo chmod 4755 ..." and "1 problem to fix before Ember can work", exit status 1. /opt/ember does not exist.
findings.evidence: appimage.sh:44 adds --no-sandbox when max_user_namespaces is 0. The doctor's sandbox row (doctor.ts:200-204) has no way to know. I ran doctorChecks with sandbox {userNamespaces:false, suidHelper:false}: it prints the FAIL row, the /opt/ember fix and "1 problem to fix before Ember can work." (scratch script doctor-sandbox.mjs). On an AppImage the files are in a nosuid squashfs, so suidHelper is always false.
findings.fix: Let the probe see that the process was started with --no-sandbox, or that APPIMAGE is set. In the AppImage case report a warn such as "Running without Chromium's sandbox (AppImage on a host with user namespaces off); use the RPM on hardened hosts", with no chown advice.

findings.title: RPM upgrade replaces files under a running Ember, and nothing tells the user to restart
findings.scenario: Ember starts at login and stays resident, so `sudo dnf upgrade ember` normally runs while the old Ember is up. rpm swaps /opt/ember/* underneath it. The old main process keeps its code in memory, but the next window it opens (settings, ask, command window) loads the new version's renderer pages and preload scripts from disk. A mixed-version Ember follows (IPC channel or payload mismatches) until someone quits and restarts it. The Windows and macOS README sections say "quit Ember" before updating; the Linux README has no update section at all. The spec has no scriptlet or notice about a running Ember.
findings.evidence: Reasoning from code: %post/%postun/%posttrans (spec lines 89-103) only refresh desktop and icon caches. renderer and preload files are read by path on window creation (app/main/windows.ts:36 and friends, loadFile). The app has no check for its own install changing. I could not run rpm here, so the failure itself is not reproduced. README.md:52 and :86 give the quit-first instruction only for Windows and macOS.
findings.fix: Add a README line for Linux ("quit Ember, then dnf upgrade; Ember starts again at your next login"). Better, have Ember compare app.getVersion() with the version in resources/app/package.json on disk when it opens a window and offer "Restart Ember". At minimum add a %posttrans echo.

findings.title: The Linux launcher shows a raw Chromium error when there is no display
findings.scenario: Someone runs `ember` from an ssh session without -X, or from a TTY. They get "ERROR:ui/ozone/platform/x11/ozone_platform_x11.cc:257] Missing X server or $DISPLAY" and "The platform failed to initialize. Exiting.", with no mention of `ember doctor`, which would have explained it. `ember doctor` itself handles the no-display case by going headless.
findings.evidence: Ran the staged binary with `env -u DISPLAY ... --ozone-platform=x11`: exit 1, only those two Chromium lines. The launcher's default path (line 25) does not check DISPLAY, while the doctor branch (line 14) does.
findings.fix: In the launcher, before the final exec: if DISPLAY is empty, print "Ember needs your desktop session (no display here). Run it from a terminal inside GNOME, or run 'ember doctor'." and exit 1.

findings.title: CI never upgrades or removes the RPM, and never builds the ember-voice-models package
findings.scenario: The release RPMs (including the `with_models` branch: %package voice-models, the %install copy and %files voice-models) are first exercised by whoever builds them for release. A mistake in that branch, in an upgrade over the previous RPM, or in the removal that leaves /opt/ember or /usr/share/ember behind would first show up on a customer's host.
findings.evidence: The package job installs once with dnf and checks files (ci.yml:147-185). It never runs scripts/voice/prepare.mjs (only the checks and eval jobs do, lines 60 and 231), so rpm.sh builds with with_models=0. There is no `dnf upgrade`, `rpm -e` or `rpm -V` step. I have no rpmbuild here, so I only read the spec.
findings.fix: In the package job: build once with a stub voice-models folder (verified markers) and install both RPMs. Then rebuild with Release 2, `dnf upgrade`, `rpm -V ember`, `rpm -e ember ember-voice-models`, and assert /opt/ember, /usr/share/ember and /usr/bin/ember are gone while /etc/ember/policy.json is kept.

findings.title: packaging/policy.example.json predates commands, WSL and SSH; copying it as-is switches those features off
findings.platforms: linux (and any remote with the file)
findings.scenario: An administrator copies the RPM's /usr/share/doc/ember/policy.example.json to /etc/ember/policy.json to start from the shipped example. A policy that exists without a `commands` key makes commands "off" for local, WSL and SSH, so the release's headline feature is silently unavailable. No row or message says why. The same file on a remote makes the helper there refuse commands.
findings.evidence: admin.ts:196-203 commandMode: source !== null and no `commands` key gives "off". The example has no commands, ssh, features.wsl or features.ssh keys. The CHANGELOG and DEVELOPING.md warn about it, but the file the RPM actually ships does not show the keys.
findings.fix: Add `"commands": {"local": "on", "wsl": "on", "ssh": "on"}` and an `"ssh": {}` example to policy.example.json, or a comment-style companion README, so the shipped example reflects the current schema.

findings.title: stage.mjs does not require the SSH/command helpers it ships (askpass.cjs, remote-link.cjs, job-host.cjs)
findings.scenario: A partial or stale dist/app, for example a build that failed after main.cjs, stages without error. The package then ships with no Windows job host or no SSH password helper or link worker, and SSH or command windows fail only at first use.
findings.evidence: COMMON_DIST (layout.mjs:30) and each target's requiredDist list main.cjs, voice.cjs, the renderer files, and ax-sidecar.cjs/desk-agent.cjs. askpass.cjs, remote-link.cjs and job-host.cjs (built by scripts/build-app.mjs and located by connections.ts:272, askpass-server.ts:264 and router.ts:821) are not listed, although stage.mjs guarantees "Every file the target needs must exist".
findings.fix: Add askpass.cjs and remote-link.cjs to the Linux and macOS requiredDist, and remote-link.cjs and job-host.cjs to Windows.

findings.title: THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES carries no licence text for @github/copilot-sdk, its runtime, sherpa-onnx or koffi's platform package
findings.scenario: The packaged notices say "(no licence file in the package; its package.json gives the licence above)" for these four packages. For MIT and Apache-2.0 software the licence text and copyright line need to travel with redistributed copies. sherpa-onnx's WebAssembly also embeds third-party runtimes (for example onnxruntime) that the notices do not list, and the 136 MB Copilot runtime is a bundled application whose own third-party notices are not shipped.
findings.evidence: grep in dist/package/ember/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES: sections at lines 133-135 (@github/copilot-sdk), 391-393 (sherpa-onnx), 424-426 (@github/copilot-sdk-linux-x64), 465-467 (@koromix/koffi-linux-x64) end in that fallback line. Apache-2.0 and MIT texts do appear for other packages, but with other copyright holders. I did not check upstream tarballs for notice files beyond what npm installed.
findings.fix: Have stage.mjs fail when a package has no licence file and a small allow-list does not supply its text. Add the missing texts (MIT for the GitHub packages, Apache-2.0 for sherpa-onnx, plus onnxruntime's notice) to THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES. Ask the upstream owners for a notices file for the runtime. This is a legal review item, not a build break.

findings.title: The shipped example policy omits the new keys, and the exec-denied message points to an 'Ember remote package' that doesn't exist
findings.scenario: An RHEL admin copies /usr/share/doc/ember/policy.example.json to /etc/ember/policy.json as the starting point. It has no commands, features.wsl/ssh or ssh section, so commands are silently off everywhere while SSH and WSL stay allowed. Nothing in the example shows how to change either. On a fapolicyd or noexec remote the user is told to 'ask its administrator… to install the Ember remote package', which does not exist; §6.6 says it is 'planned'.
findings.evidence: packaging/policy.example.json holds only the pre-release keys and is installed by packaging/rpm/ember.spec:76 and :112. ssh-errors.ts:60 (execDenied) and docs §4.8 line 505 quote the 'remote package' sentence while COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md:628 says a root-owned remote package is planned.
findings.fix: Add features.wsl, features.ssh, commands and ssh (with allowedHosts and desktop) to the example, with a comment key or a README beside it saying that a policy without `commands` turns commands off. Reword the message to the fapolicyd or noexec fix only, until the package ships.

findings.title: After the merge nothing runs the SSH, WSL and commands integration suites on PRs, main or release tags; the primary platform's old ssh client is never exercised; Linux arm64 is untested
findings.scenario: remote.yml triggers on push only for branches `ember-improve/20261022-sshwsl-*`, dispatch, and a weekly macOS-only cron. After merge, regressions in script(1), sshd, the bootstrap, WSL and PowerShell commands are not caught by PRs or the v* release tag (ci.yml runs only unit tests for them). The client side is always the runner's OpenSSH 9.6, but the RHEL 8 PC uses OpenSSH 8.0 (askpass through DISPLAY, no SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE), which no job runs. The test sshds disable password and keyboard-interactive auth, so password, passphrase and 2FA prompts through a real ssh are only unit tested. Linux arm64 remotes are advertised and shipped (Node arm64 pinned, koffi arm64) but no job installs or runs one.
findings.evidence: on.push.branches in remote.yml:12-14; no pull_request trigger; schedule runs only ssh-macos (`if: github.event_name == 'schedule' || …`). ssh-linux and ssh-el8 install the client from the Ubuntu 24.04 runner (ssh-el8 uses Rocky 8 only as the server); sshd configs set `PasswordAuthentication no` and `KbdInteractiveAuthentication no`. `grep -i arm remote.yml` finds nothing.
findings.fix: Add `pull_request` (paths-filtered to app/main/{commands,remote,wsl,targets}, app/remote, scripts/package) and `tags: [v*]` triggers. Run ssh-transport inside a rockylinux:8 container as the client as well. Add a password or keyboard-interactive sshd case (sshpass or an askpass fake) and an ubuntu-24.04-arm job.

findings.title: Downloaded Node archives in userData are never pruned
findings.scenario: Every Ember release that bumps the pinned Node leaves the previous archive (32 MB xz, or 58 MB gz) per target in ~/.config/ember/remote/runtime/ for ever, including after 'Forget'. Over a few releases a user accumulates hundreds of MB.
findings.evidence: ensureRuntime writes <userData>/remote/runtime/<file> and only checks cachedOk for the pinned file; connections.ts:394 is the only user and nothing deletes other files in that folder.
findings.fix: After a successful ensureRuntime, delete files in the folder that aren't the pinned name (and any *.part older than a day). Mention the folder in the README's uninstall list.

findings.title: Duplicate sshClientRow in ssh-config.ts is dead code and disagrees with the doctor row (fail vs warn)
findings.scenario: A future caller of the unused helper would make a missing or old OpenSSH a 'fail' in `ember doctor`, although docs §5 say it is only ever a warning (SSH is optional) and targets/doctor.ts:50 does that.
findings.evidence: grep finds sshClientRow(os, path, v) used only by test/unit/ssh-config.test.ts; the setup check and doctor use targets/doctor.ts sshClientRow. The two return different statuses for the same input.
findings.fix: Delete the ssh-config.ts copy and its tests, or have doctor.ts call it with the warn mapping.
